provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after quaesumus; 1862 sets a colon after innititur where the 1962 sets a comma; 1862 spells coelestis, the 1962 caelestis; 1862 conclusion is the short cue 'Per Dominum.' where the 1962 expands it. Corroboration: 1604 at lines 14579-14587, '[F]amiliam tua, quaesumus Domine, continua pietate custodi: vt quae in sola spe gratiae caelestis innititur, tua semper protectione muniatur. Per Dominum.'.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Familiam tuam, quaesumus, Domine, continua pietate custodi: ut, quae in sola
spe gratiae caelestis innititur, tua semper protectione muniatur. Per
Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in
unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
